summary: First checkpoint of the blueprint for Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology and Iwasawa cohomology, within RS-08's boundaries. L0: the p-adic completion of a multiplicative group and its comparison with the tensor product (true for global units and S-units, false for local multiplicative groups and for F^×), the Kummer maps along the μ_{p^m} tower, the Mittag-Leffler bookkeeping, the identification H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} and its S-unit form H^1(G_{F,S}, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^×. L2: the generic Selmer-kernel API (local conditions, strict and relaxed modifications, change of conditions, functoriality, propagation, the passage V → T, W with saturation), the unramified and Greenberg conditions, Galois Selmer groups, Pontryagin duals and coranks, and the elliptic p^∞-Selmer group. Two new findings in RJW are recorded.

nodes.title: p-adic completion of an abelian group
nodes.statement: For an abelian group A (written additively; A = Fˣ through Additive) and a prime p, Â = lim_m A/p^mA, Mathlib's AdicCompletion of A for the ideal (p) ⊆ ℤ, with the canonical map A → Â. It is a module over AdicCompletion(p)ℤ ≅ ℤ_p. For finitely generated A the natural map ℤ_p ⊗ A → Â is an isomorphism. In general it is neither injective nor surjective, and Â is the object Rubin writes K^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p.
hypotheses: p prime; no finiteness on A for the definition.
Rubin's Definition I.6.2 double-dual completion agrees with this Â for finitely generated A and whenever every A/p^mA is finite; Example I.2.1 uses the inverse limit, which is the object used here.
proofSteps: Definition: AdicCompletion (span {p}) A.
ℤ_p ⊗ A ≅ Â for finitely generated A: AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_bijective_of_finite_of_isNoetherian over the Noetherian ring ℤ.
AdicCompletion(p)ℤ ≅ ℤ_p: both are lim ℤ/p^m (PadicInt.toZModPow).
acceptance: The failure for infinitely generated A is the reason the stage forbids replacing (Fˣ)^ by Fˣ ⊗ ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Completion of global units
nodes.statement: For a number field F, the unit group E_F = 𝓞_F^× is finitely generated, so ℤ_p ⊗ E_F ≅ Ê_F; and the map Ê_F → (F^×)^ induced by E_F ⊆ F^× is injective, because E_F ∩ (F^×)^{p^m} = E_F^{p^m}: a p^m-th root in F of a unit is a unit.
hypotheses: F a number field, p prime, m ≥ 0.
proofSteps: E_F is finitely generated by Dirichlet's theorem (NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod: every unit is torsion times a product of fundamental units); apply padic-completion.
If x ∈ F^× and x^{p^m} = u ∈ E_F, then x and x^{−1} are integral over 𝓞_F (IsIntegral.of_pow), so x ∈ E_F.
Hence the subspace topology on E_F from the p-adic topology of F^× is its own p-adic topology, and the completion map is injective.
acceptance: The image is closed but not all of (F^×)^; the quotient (F^×)^/Ê_F involves the ideal group.

nodes.title: Completion of S-units
nodes.statement: For a number field F and a finite set S of places containing the archimedean ones, 𝓞_{F,S}^× is finitely generated, so ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^× ≅ (𝓞_{F,S}^×)^, and (𝓞_{F,S}^×)^ → (F^×)^ is injective.
hypotheses: S finite, containing the archimedean places.
proofSteps: Finite generation is Dirichlet's S-unit theorem (requested from Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields).
An element of F^× whose p^m-th power is an S-unit has valuation zero outside S, so it is an S-unit; conclude as in units-completion.
acceptance: For S = S_∞ this is units-completion.

nodes.title: Completion of a local multiplicative group
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, with K^× = π^ℤ × 𝓞_K^× and 𝓞_K^× = μ_{q−1} × U^1_K. Then (K^×)^ ≅ ℤ_p × (𝓞_K^×)^, where (𝓞_K^×)^ = U^1_K if ℓ = p (a finitely generated ℤ_p-module) and (𝓞_K^×)^ = μ_{p^∞}(K) if ℓ ≠ p (U^1_K is pro-ℓ, hence p-divisible). The map K^× ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → (K^×)^ is surjective but not injective, so for local fields the completion does not agree with the algebraic tensor product.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_ℓ finite, ℓ any prime (ℓ = p allowed).
proofSteps: The decomposition K^× = π^ℤ × μ_{q−1} × U^1_K and the structure of U^1_K come from Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 (requested).
Completion commutes with finite products; ℤ̂ = ℤ_p; μ_{q−1} contributes its p-part; U^1_K is already p-adically complete (ℓ = p) or p-divisible (ℓ ≠ p).
Non-injectivity for ℓ = p: U^1_K ⊇ ℤ_p, and ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → ℤ_p kills a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a, which is nonzero for a ∉ ℚ because ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p ⊆ ℚ_p ⊗_ℚ ℚ_p.
acceptance: For ℓ ≠ p, the kernel contains U^1_K ⊗ ℤ_p ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Finiteness of local power classes
nodes.statement: For K a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ and n ≥ 1, K^×/(K^×)^n is finite. Hence H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) is finite, (K^×)^ is profinite, and lim_m K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} carries the inverse-limit topology of finite discrete groups.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_ℓ finite; n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: K^×/(K^×)^n is a quotient of ℤ/n × 𝓞_K^×/(𝓞_K^×)^n, and (𝓞_K^×)^n is open of finite index by Hensel's lemma (LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1).
H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) ≅ K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} by Kummer theory (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9).
acceptance: For global F, F^×/(F^×)^n is infinite; this is why the global limit is not profinite.

nodes.title: Kummer maps along the μ_{p^m} tower
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with p invertible in K and m ≥ 0. The p-th power map μ_{p^{m+1}} → μ_{p^m} carries the Kummer class κ_{p^{m+1}}(a) ∈ H^1(G_K, μ_{p^{m+1}}) to κ_{p^m}(a) for every a ∈ K^×.
hypotheses: p invertible in K (Tau Ceti's hypothesis IsUnit (n : K)).
proofSteps: (x ↦ x^p on μ_{p^{m+1}} and on (Kˢ)ˣ, identity on the right-hand (Kˢ)ˣ) is a map of Kummer short exact sequences, because (x^p)^{p^m} = x^{p^{m+1}}.
δ⁰ is natural for maps of short exact sequences (TauCeti.ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact.explicitDelta0_coeffMap), and kummerMap is δ⁰ read on Kˣ (TauCeti.kummerMap_apply).
acceptance: For m = 0 the target is H^1(G_K, μ_1) = 0.

nodes.title: The limit Kummer map
nodes.statement: For a field K with p invertible, κ_∞ : lim_m K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} → lim_m H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) is the limit of the Kummer class maps (TauCeti.kummerClassMap) along the tower of kummer-level-compatibility. It is injective, and bijective once the finite-level Kummer maps are surjective (Hilbert 90, ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9).
hypotheses: p invertible in K.
proofSteps: Levelwise injectivity (TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective) passes to inverse limits.
Levelwise bijectivity (Hilbert 90) gives an isomorphism of inverse systems, hence of limits.
acceptance: The limit is taken of groups; topologies are compared in padic-kummer-identification.

nodes.title: The system μ_{p^m}(K) is Mittag-Leffler
nodes.statement: For any field K, the inverse system m ↦ μ_{p^m}(K) = H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) with the p-th power maps consists of finite groups (at most p^m elements), so it is Mittag-Leffler and lim^1_m H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) = 0.
hypotheses: K any field with p invertible.
proofSteps: μ_{p^m}(K) has at most p^m elements (card_rootsOfUnity).
A system of finite sets is Mittag-Leffler (CategoryTheory.Functor.isMittagLeffler_of_exists_finite_range).
lim^1 of a Mittag-Leffler system of groups vanishes (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1).
acceptance: This is the finiteness hypothesis of Rubin's Proposition B.2.3 for i = 1.

nodes.title: The p-adic Kummer identification
nodes.statement: For a field K with p invertible, H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim_m K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} = (K^×)^, where ℤ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^m} is a compact coefficient module and H^1 is continuous-cochain cohomology (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1). The map is H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) → lim_m H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}), an isomorphism because the Milnor term lim^1 H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) vanishes, followed by κ_∞^{−1}. It is an algebraic isomorphism for every K; when every K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} is finite (local fields) both sides are profinite and it is a homeomorphism. It is compatible with restriction and with corestriction versus the norm for finite separable extensions.
hypotheses: p invertible in K. No finite generation of K^× is assumed; the target is the completion, not K^× ⊗ ℤ_p.
proofSteps: Milnor sequence 0 → lim^1 H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) → H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) → lim H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) → 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1; Rubin Proposition B.2.3).
roots-of-unity-mittag-leffler kills the lim^1 term.
kummer-limit-map identifies the limit with (K^×)^.
For local K, local-power-class-finite makes both sides profinite, and a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff groups is a homeomorphism.
acceptance: For K = ℚ the identification holds with the completion, and ℚ^× ⊗ ℤ_p → H^1(G_ℚ, ℤ_p(1)) is not surjective (sourceIssues E1).

nodes.title: The Kummer identification for S-units
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞. Then H^1(G_{F,S}, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^×, compatibly with restriction to finite extensions inside F_S and with corestriction versus the norm.
hypotheses: S ⊇ {v | p∞}, so μ_{p^m} is a G_{F,S}-module and p is an S-unit.
proofSteps: The Kummer sequence for G_{F,S}: 0 → 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m → H^1(G_{F,S}, μ_{p^m}) → Pic(𝓞_{F,S})[p^m] → 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3).
Pass to the limit: roots-of-unity-mittag-leffler removes lim^1 H^0; the terms 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m are finite; lim_m Pic[p^m] = T_p Pic = 0 because Pic(𝓞_{F,S}) is finite.
lim 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m = ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^× (s-units-completion).
acceptance: This is the finite-level statement behind Burungale–Tian's units-kummer item; the tower limit belongs to L3.

nodes.title: Which inverse-limit hypotheses hold
nodes.statement: For the towers used in this roadmap: (a) for every field K, lim^1_m μ_{p^m}(K) = 0; (b) for K local, every H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) is finite, so the H^1 system is Mittag-Leffler and H^2(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) = lim_m H^2(G_K, μ_{p^m}); (c) for G_{F,S} with S ⊇ {v | p∞}, every H^1(G_{F,S}, μ_{p^m}) is finite, with the same consequence; (d) for the full G_F of a number field, H^1(G_F, μ_{p^m}) = F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} is infinite, and no Mittag-Leffler argument is available for H^2(G_F, ℤ_p(1)).
hypotheses: p invertible; F a number field; S finite.
proofSteps: (a) roots-of-unity-mittag-leffler.
(b) local-power-class-finite and Rubin Proposition B.2.3 with i = 2.
(c) The Kummer sequence of s-unit-kummer-identification has finite outer terms.
(d) F^× contains a free abelian group on the primes.
acceptance: Consumers must cite (b) or (c) before interchanging H^2 and limits.

nodes.title: Selmer data
nodes.statement: Selmer data over a commutative ring R indexed by a set of places ι: a global R-module H (for example H^1(G_{K,Σ}, M)), local R-modules H_v (for example H^1(K_v, M)), R-linear localisation maps res_v : H → H_v, and local conditions L_v ⊆ H_v (R-submodules). Modifications replace the conditions: relaxed (L_v = H_v) on a set of places, strict (L_v = 0) on a set of places.
hypotheses: The data are module-theoretic, so the same API serves discrete (Tau Ceti), compact and rational coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1).
proofSteps: Structure with fields glob, loc, res, cond; modifications by withCond.
acceptance: Mazur–Rubin's F^b_a(n) is withCond with strict conditions at a and relaxed ones at b; transverse conditions belong to EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.1.

nodes.statement: If L_v ≤ L'_v for all v, then Sel_L ⊆ Sel_{L'} and the sequence 0 → Sel_L → Sel_{L'} → ∏_v L'_v/L_v is exact.
hypotheses: Same global module and localisation maps for both conditions.
proofSteps: Monotonicity; a class of Sel_{L'} lies in Sel_L iff each res_v c lies in L_v, that is, iff its image in ∏ L'_v/L_v vanishes.
acceptance: Mazur–Rubin (2.4) is the case L' = L relaxed at the primes dividing n/m.

nodes.title: Functoriality of Selmer modules

hypotheses: Compatibility squares and inclusion of conditions.
proofSteps: Chase: res'_v(f c) = f_v(res_v c) ∈ f_v(L_v) ⊆ L'_v.

nodes.title: Propagating local conditions
nodes.statement: Along a coefficient map inducing g : H^1(K_v, X) → H^1(K_v, Y), a condition L ⊆ H^1(K_v, X) propagates forwards to g(L) (quotients T ↠ T/IT, V → W), and a condition L' ⊆ H^1(K_v, Y) propagates backwards to g^{−1}(L') (submodules T[I] ↪ T, T → V). The two form a Galois connection.
hypotheses: Any R-linear g.
proofSteps: Image and preimage of submodules; Galois connection Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap.
acceptance: Mazur–Rubin propagate by image to T/IT and by inverse image to T[I].

nodes.title: From V to T and W; saturation
nodes.statement: Given L_V ⊆ H^1(K_v, V), put L_T = inverse image under H^1(K_v, T) → H^1(K_v, V) and L_W = image under H^1(K_v, V) → H^1(K_v, W) (Rubin's H^1_f(K_v, T), H^1_f(K_v, W)). Then H^1(K_v, T)/L_T is torsion-free (L_T is saturated) and L_W is divisible.
hypotheses: T a finitely generated free ℤ_p- or O-module with continuous action, V = T[1/p], W = V/T; L_V a ℚ_p-subspace.
proofSteps: If n·x ∈ L_T with n ≠ 0 then n·x ↦ n·y ∈ L_V, and y ∈ L_V as L_V is a ℚ_p-subspace, so x ∈ L_T.
L_W is the image of a ℚ_p-vector space, hence divisible.
The maps H^1(T) → H^1(V) → H^1(W) come from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1.
acceptance: The saturation of the condition on T and the divisibility on W are separate statements, as the stage asks.

nodes.title: The unramified condition
nodes.statement: For a decomposition group G_v with inertia subgroup I_v and a G_v-module B, H^1_ur(K_v, B) = ker(H^1(G_v, B) → H^1(I_v, B)). By inflation–restriction it is the image of H^1(G_v/I_v, B^{I_v}), and for procyclic G_v/I_v generated by Fr it is B^{I_v}/(Fr − 1)B^{I_v}.
hypotheses: B discrete, a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, or a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-space (Rubin Lemma I.3.2).
proofSteps: Kernel of restriction to inertia.
Inflation–restriction (Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 5; Rubin Proposition B.2.5(i)).
H^1(Ẑ, C) = C/(Fr − 1)C by evaluation at Fr (Rubin Lemma B.2.8).
acceptance: Unramified B: H^1_ur = B/(Fr − 1)B.

nodes.title: Greenberg's local condition
nodes.statement: For a decomposition group G_v at p with inertia I_v and a G_v-stable submodule F^+M ⊆ M, L^Gr_v = ker(H^1(G_v, M) → H^1(I_v, M/F^+M)). F^+M need only be stable under G_v, not under the global Galois group.
hypotheses: F^+ stable under G_v; for W = V/T use the image F^+W of F^+V.
proofSteps: Kernel of the composite of restriction to I_v and the map induced by M → M/F^+M.
acceptance: For M = W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n) over ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+ with Fil^1 = W_n (n ≥ 1) or 0 (n ≤ 0), L^Gr is everything or the unramified condition (RJW §13.5.2).

nodes.title: Galois-cohomological Selmer groups
nodes.statement: For a number field K, a finite set Σ of places containing those above p∞ and the ramified primes, and a coefficient module M (discrete, compact or rational), Sel_L(K, M) is the Selmer module of the data H = H^1(G_{K,Σ}, M), H_v = H^1(K_v, M), res_v the localisation (restriction to a decomposition group), with local conditions L_v for v ∈ Σ. It equals the classes of H^1(K, M) that are unramified outside Σ and satisfy L_v at Σ (Rubin Lemma I.5.3).
hypotheses: Σ ⊇ {v | p∞} ∪ {ramified primes}; the conditions at v ∉ Σ are unramified.
proofSteps: G_{K,Σ}, decomposition groups and localisation maps come from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3.
Rubin's Lemma I.5.3: the unramified conditions outside Σ cut out H^1(K_Σ/K, M) inside H^1(K, M).
acceptance: Enlarging Σ with unramified conditions does not change the group.

nodes.title: Pontryagin duals with the contragredient action

nodes.title: The p^∞-Selmer group of an elliptic curve
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and a prime p, Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) is the Galois Selmer group of M = E[p^∞] with local conditions the images of E(F_v) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p under the local Kummer maps; equivalently ker(H^1(F, E[p^∞]) → ∏_v H^1(F_v, E)[p^∞]), and the direct limit of the Sel_{p^m}. It sits in 0 → E(F) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p → Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) → Ш(E/F)[p^∞] → 0.
hypotheses: E/F elliptic; the finite-level Selmer groups and local Kummer maps come from Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7.
proofSteps: Instantiate galois-selmer-group; identify the local conditions with the Kummer images; pass to the direct limit over m.
acceptance: The Bloch–Kato comparison of these conditions on V_pE belongs to L4.

sourceIssues.locator: §10.5, display (10.7), printed p. 52 (arXiv v2), and (10.8), printed p. 53
sourceIssues.printed: The source treats inverse limits over m ≥ 1 as exact and obtains the Kummer isomorphism δ : F× ⊗ Zp ∼−→ H1(F, Zp(1)). (10.7) It then applies the same procedure with Qp replacing Q and with F replaced by a finite extension Kn of Qp, for n ≥ 1, to obtain K×n ⊗ Zp ≅ H1(Kn, Zp(1)).
sourceIssues.correction: δ : lim_m F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} ≅ H^1(F, ℤ_p(1)), with the p-adic completion (Rubin's F^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p) in place of F^× ⊗ ℤ_p; likewise for K_n. The limit step holds because lim^1_m μ_{p^m}(F) = 0 (finite groups; Rubin Proposition B.2.3), not because inverse limits are exact.
sourceIssues.reason: For a number field F, F^× contains a free abelian group on infinitely many primes, and a p-adic Cauchy sequence such as ∏_{i≤m} ℓ_i^{p^i} involves infinitely many primes, so it is not in the image of F^× ⊗ ℤ_p: the map is not surjective. For K/ℚ_p finite, U^1_K ⊇ ℤ_p and ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → ℤ_p kills a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a, which is nonzero for a ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℚ since ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p embeds in ℚ_p ⊗_ℚ ℚ_p: the map is not injective. Inverse limits of abelian groups are not exact in general; the lim^1 term must be shown to vanish.

sourceIssues.printed: The source calls V p-ordinary in Greenberg’s sense when V admits a finite saturated GQ-invariant filtration Fil^i. It requires IQp inside GQp to act on Fil^i/Fil^{i+1} through the cyclotomic character raised to the ith power. It defines L^Gr_vp := ker(H1(Fvp, W) → H1(Ivp, W) → H1(Ivp, W/Fil1W)).
sourceIssues.correction: The filtration Fil^i V must be stable under G_{ℚ_p} (a decomposition group at p), not under G_ℚ, as in Greenberg's [Gre89]; the local condition L^Gr only uses its restriction to G_{ℚ_p}.
sourceIssues.reason: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ with good ordinary reduction at p and without complex multiplication, V_pE is irreducible under G_ℚ, so it has no nontrivial G_ℚ-invariant filtration, yet it is Greenberg's basic ordinary example, with Fil^1 the line coming from the connected component of E[p^∞] over ℤ_p, which is only G_{ℚ_p}-stable. As printed, Definition 13.19(1) and Conjecture 13.21 would exclude it. The notes' own example V = ℚ_p(n) in §13.5.2 is one-dimensional and unaffected.
